correctness.rationale: For all fixed integers p and q at least three, normalizing two independent Gaussian pairs proves Haar factorization W~Uniform[0,1] independent of angular distances; conditioning on W yields the exact CDF. A unique angular corner attains the sharp minimum c, with exactly pq deepest directions. The first-order Taylor expansion has strictly positive angular slopes; tent-domain rescaling proves the cubic term and fourth-order remainder uniformly for each fixed pair. An independent 16-corner tangent-simplex computation gives the coefficient 512 divided by three times pi squared. Standalone verify.py passed seven pair near-tail integrations, the exact cross-polytope check and three full-CDF direct sampling comparisons.

The exact full CDF and positive sharp cubic coefficient quantify worst-direction robustness for every pair of regular orthogonal polygon rings, including exact cross-polytope consistency. This is a natural complete distribution beyond the radius and differentiates near-deep-hole volumes; not merely a renaming of the facet inradius.
